Prose

A wrapper for long-form content you do not write the markup for — a rendered Markdown post, CMS HTML, release notes. Links inside it get the Text Link underline look without being Text Links, because Markdown writes its own <a>.

Links only, for now2 modesToken-driven

Preview

Plain <a> elements, exactly as a Markdown renderer writes them. Hover one: the underline goes from 50% to full colour and from 1px to 1.5px. Tab to one for the focus ring.

Style elements on hover, focus and more using pseudo-classes, like :hover, :focus and :first-child. Read the IronPDF docs for the full list, or start from the HTML to PDF tutorial.

Dark

dark moves the links to the dark tokens. The text around them is the page’s — Prose styles links and nothing else.

On a dark band the text and its links move to the dark tokens together — see the release notes for what changed.

Why not just Text Link

Use Text Link whenever you write the link yourself. Prose is for when you cannot: Markdown and CMS content produce bare <a> tags, and Text Link’s styles are scoped to the markup it renders, so they never reach them. Left bare, those links render as the browser’s blue, solidly underlined, purple once visited. Prose gives them the same values as TextLink variant="underline" — and the same as Figma’s Typography/link-underline text style, which is how a designer marks a link inside a paragraph. A real <TextLink> placed inside Prose keeps its own look.
